The derivation begins by treating perception-time not as a monolithic delay, but as a composite operator \mathcal{T} acting on sensory manifolds. By isolating the muscular and sensorial components, we establish a dual basis for measuring cognitive load. The reproductive association kernel K(x,y) then acts upon these processed states, retrieving probable objects based on historical similarity. This forms the foundational prior for any subsequent inference. When concatenated into habit chains, these retrieved objects dictate state transitions. Mathematically, the habit chain is a sequence of conditional probabilities P(H_{t+1}|H_t), where each transition is gated by the plasticity of the neural substrate. The duality lies between the immediate, high-frequency fluctuations of perception-time and the slow, low-frequency drift of habit formation. Failure modes emerge when the environment shifts rapidly, causing the similarity kernel to return spurious matches, thereby breaking the habit chain. The principle of transferred relations ensures that abstracted features from one domain can stabilize another, preventing total systemic collapse during novelty.

The concatenation of habits directly inherits from Aristotle's enchainment of actions, formalized here through modern Markovian lenses, bridging classical empiricism with contemporary stochastic state-space modeling. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires recognizing that their habit chains operate on different internal clocks. An agent's expectant attention modulates their perception-time, effectively creating a localized distortion in the shared temporal manifold. Predicting an opponent involves reverse-engineering their reproductive kernel—determining which past similarities they prioritize. If we can force a mismatch between their expected habit-chain transition and the actual environmental state, we induce a catastrophic failure in their decision loop.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring the perception-time operator does not perfectly correlate with the habit-chain transition probabilities. If reaction-time becomes entirely predictable by the current habit state, the system loses adaptive capacity. Leakage vetoes occur when the reproductive kernel overfits to recent noise rather than deep structural similarities. We must continuously inject orthogonal perturbations to verify that the transferred relations remain robust against adversarial manipulation of the sensory input layer.
